resolvedQuestions.text: What drove the measured result (K=56, M=56, A=55, B=47, W=8, L=0, F=1, p_win=0.003906)?
How can grader accuracy be raised or cost lowered?
Where else in .skilled would the same invented-name judgment pay off?
How can the measurement be made more trustworthy?
What would a default-on integration need, cost, and risk?

keyFindings.text: 56 outputs = 42 honest (21 fixtures x run1/run2) + 14 careless run3; the 9 yes labels are exactly the nine hallucinating run3 files; 5 run3 answers are careless but clean.
A=55: all 47 no rows right, 8/9 yes rows right; the miss is harder-normalize-path.run3 (nouls 0.43/0.43/0.40, invented require + splitOnSlashes), a threshold false negative.
F=1 comes from validate-semver.run3 (0.55/0.41/0.54, two yes votes, one dissent); every other row voted unanimously.
Noul separation: no-class median 0.07 / p95 0.23 / max 0.43; yes-class median 0.71 / min 0.40; only 8 of 168 calls in [0.40,0.60).
Baseline is majority (no) because checkRight 22 < majorityRight 47; majority never says yes, so the 8 caught yes rows are the only wins (W=8) and L=0 is structural.

The check's 22 reproduces exactly in memory (tp=9 tn=13 fp=34 fn=0) and is an allowlist artifact: 0 of 21 fixtures carry an allowlist, so every extracted token is unverified and 34 of 47 honest rows are flagged.
The grader sees task+visibleSpec+output and can tell task-provided names from invented ones; the check cannot, which is exactly where the 34 fp and the grader's 47/47 specificity come from.
All five keep checks pass: coverage 560>=504, p_loss=1.0, margin 80>=56, sign 2^-8<0.05, flips 10<=168; headroom gate 470>504 false so the arm opened.
169 calls (1 auth + 3x56), 0 unmeasured, ~93,003 estimated input tokens, app latency p50 326 ms / p95 434 ms / max 648 ms, auth 614 ms.
0/21 fixtures carry allowlists; populating them repairs check specificity, anchors the Claude grader rubric, and lets buildState pass ground truth to the jev grader — the top structural lever.
Cascade routes 43/56 rows today (130 vs 169 calls, 23% saving) because check fn=0; saving grows once allowlists cut the 34 false positives (unmeasured).
Threshold 0.42 would fix the corpus miss with no no-row flip, but margin is one row and 0.03 noul: held-out hypothesis, not a patch.
In the --grader llm path a dispatch or parse failure yields score 0.0 / parse_status failed, reading as maximal hallucination (D4 weight 0.15).
dispute.cjs escalates low-confidence D4 calls to an adversarial second call with median+dispute; the jev arm has no analogue; 8/168 calls sit in [0.40,0.60).
Review findings already promise the property (paths exist, citations verified, no hallucinated issues) but enforce it by self-attestation; a jev name-existence pass makes it measured. Highest stake.
reviewer-scorer.cjs grades reviewer-prompt fixtures with expectedVerdict/expectedFindings; four reviewer fixtures already in the corpus; D4 seat exists in the same scorer.
cite-drift-scan.mjs covers only <path>:<line> citation shapes and runs its own jev question; prose flag/function claims are uncovered — the D4 complement, as an advisory doc lint.
Deep-loop evidence files cite file:line at high volume; dead citations partially covered, never-existed targets the complement; lower stake than review findings.
cli-classifier registers one transport (cli-jev) and says future classifiers join as modes; a name-existence mode gives all surfaces one route instead of per-feature prompts.
Not for forward-looking planning docs (they legitimately name future artifacts); any code-answer adoption needs populated allowlists or it repeats the empty-allowlist false-positive trap.
Keep rule pre-registered 2026-09-29 before any model run; REQ-005 voids earlier verdicts if changed; power floor documented; applied exactly.
Labels are one delegated opinion: fresh Opus 5.5 medium arbiter per 042 ADR-001, blind, no second rater or adjudication of the one disagreement.
Rows cluster by fixture (42 honest = 21x2; 9 yes = 9 fixtures; W+L=8); sign test assumes independence. Accuracy 55/56 CP95 [0.9045,0.9995] hides sensitivity 8/9 [0.5175,0.9972].
Nominal, not family-wise: Bonferroni k=15 threshold 0.003333, k=22 0.002273, p_win 0.00390625 above both; P(>=1 false keep in 15 indep tests) = 0.5367.
Check column flags a superset of the jev question scope because allowlists are empty; B is majority, so the 22 is not a same-question comparator; allowlist population makes the bar harder.
Requalification compares provider/model only; labels sha is printed/recorded but never compared. Cache grader build hash placeholder mitigated by model-name+prompt-sha composite.
Single recorded execution; 027 rerun precedent exists; the one flip shows boundary sampling noise; verdict stability unmeasured for 024.
Receipts are strong (labels sha, calls.jsonl, strict parsing, payload gate, byte-identical skips); gaps are report surfacing.
Corpus tests one hallucination family on cooperative text; no other planted hallucination kinds and no adversarial outputs, though the harness has injection defenses.
The keep covers the jev column only; the llm grader is a different implementation never measured by this arm; keep rule applies per backend column; wiring a jev kind is a later operator-opened phase.
A default-on grader must first gain an unmeasured/unavailable representation; today dispatch or parse failure becomes score 0.0, deliberately left unchanged by 024 D1.
Defaults are hermetic (pattern, noop) and reports stamp scoringMethod+grader; default-on changes what every run measures and needs versioning plus re-baselining.

Family-collision guard refuses same-family llm grading without explicit override; jev gate skips without credential; default-on needs a stated independent grader model and documented degraded mode, no silent mock fallback.

One grader call per scored output per uncached pass; harness cache makes repeats free; recorded jev reference 169 calls / ~93k est. tokens for 56 outputs; no per-run cost cap (fanout cost-unit guard precedent).
The llm rubric scores against allowlist.cli_flags/symbols; all 21 fixtures carry none; populate before default-on or the grader runs anchorless.
Blast radius is advisory: the auto workflow can only recommend, cannot invoke promotion or create approval receipts (test asserts); outcome enum includes advisoryOnly.
Repeatability tolerance precedent (0.03, sub-tolerance deltas read as ties) encodes single-sample noise concerns; default-on D4 adds sampled noise to 15% of the weighted score.
Measurement trust debt (single-labeler labels, clustered rows, nominal significance, one hallucination family) would circulate at larger scale with default-on.

ruledOutDirections.text: Reading 'deterministic check 22 of 56' as the check's realistic ceiling
ruledOutDirections.reason: It is the check with its allowlist input empty, which the fixture corpus guarantees.

ruledOutDirections.text: Retuning the 0.5 threshold on this corpus' own evidence
ruledOutDirections.reason: Post-hoc, one-row margin (0.03 noul); threshold policy belongs in a fresh held-out agreement run.
